{{Short description|British mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2024}}
'''John David Philip Meldrum''' (18 July 1940 in [[Rabat]], Morocco; died 9 August 2018 in [[Edinburgh]], Scotland) was a British mathematician. Meldrum was an [[Abstract Algebra|algebraist]] and his research was mostly related to [[group theory]].{{r|blms}}

== Biography ==
Meldrum was born in Rabat, Morocco.{{r|blms}}

In 1964 he was appointed as a supernumerary fellow and college lecturer in mathematics at [[Emmanuel College, Cambridge|Emmanuel College]].{{r|blms}} Meldrum received his PhD from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1967 on the topic of "''Central Series in Wreath Products''". His supervisor was [[Derek Roy Taunt]].{{r|mg}}
 
In 1969 he became a lecturer for mathematics at the [[University of Edinburgh]] and in 1982 he was appointed there as a senior lecturer.{{r|blms}}

He died on 9 August 2018 in Edinburgh after a battle with the [[Parkinson's disease]].{{r|blms}}
